preamble: Deglottalization: the velar ejective [kʼ] loses its glottalic airstream and merges with plain [k]. In Akkadian, Geers's law turns ḳ (Proto-Semitic *kʼ) into k when the same root also contains ṣ, which outranks it in stability, regardless of position. Fallon (2002) documents full or partial mergers of ejectives with plain stops in Omotic (Yemsa word-initially), Jicaquean and Lezgian dialects. Modern Hebrew and Cypriot Maronite Arabic reach k in two steps, through uvular q (*kʼ > q > k); each step is filed separately. In Chechen and Ingush, *kʼ after x lost its glottalization but stayed voiceless, while single non-initial kʼ elsewhere became g.

examples.note: ḳ > k next to ṣ; Arabic qaṣara 'shorten, restrict' keeps both emphatics. A rare exception is ḳaṣû beside regular kaṣû 'cold' (Streck 2011).
